headline: One Cruise Giant Outpollutes Europe’s Cars
lede: Carnival’s ships emitted nearly ten times as much sulphur oxide around European coasts as the continent’s passenger cars in 2017. The comparison puts bunker fuel, weak maritime rules, and port-city exposure squarely on the record.

headline: AI Designs a CPU From First Principles
lede: Frostbite is an AI-co-designed CPU architecture built around explicit dependencies, local computation, and single-use values. Its pre-silicon results are striking, but the silicon—and the stronger comparisons—have yet to arrive.

headline: Understanding Begins With a Simple Explanation
lede: Richard Feynman treated explanation as a private test of knowledge, not merely a public performance. Simplifying an idea can expose the gap between fluent language and genuine understanding—provided the audience and the missing nuance are kept in view.

headline: Critical OpenSSL Overflow Gets a Guardrail
lede: CVE-2026-121481 targets an encoding path with invalid lengths, null buffers, and integer overflow conditions. The proposed fix rejects dangerous inputs and adds related validation; treat the advisory as a patching priority once the official guidance lands.

headline: How Oxygène Made Room for Synthesizers
lede: In 1976, Jean-Michel Jarre assembled Oxygène from analogue synthesizers, drum machines, tape, and a small home studio. The forthcoming anniversary editions return to those original eight-track sources while preserving a record of technical limitation turned melodic landmark.

headline: A Sokoban Solver Finds New Routes Through Walls
lede: Soksolv combines deadlock pruning, corral analysis, novelty search, factoring, and parallel lanes to clear levels that had resisted published solvers. Its 430-agent development process is as notable as the benchmark results: machine-assisted iteration, bounded by human testing and expensive compute.

headline: A Browser Tool Maps the Sound of Tinnitus
lede: This small web project narrows a perceived tinnitus pitch through repeated tone comparisons, level calibration, and octave checks. It keeps results local and reports a useful range—not a diagnosis or a promise of false precision.

headline: Silicon Valley’s Contradictions Have a Business Model
lede: The article reads tech leaders’ conflicting claims about AI, risk, and misconduct as products of incentives, groupthink, and founder mythology. The harder question is whether these contradictions signal hypocrisy—or the ordinary collision of public principles with private ambition.
pullquote: When technological necessity becomes a business argument, contradiction starts to sound like strategy.

headline: FFmpeg Gauss Ships Another Essential Toolkit
lede: FFmpeg 9.1 updates the libraries beneath modern audio and video workflows. Fetch the source, verify its signatures—including post-quantum options—and remember: stable releases serve integrators; the development branch moves faster.

headline: USB Fits Inside a One-Kilobyte Chip
lede: The µ-Wire project pushes USB and WS2812 control onto an ATtiny10 with only 1 KB of flash and 32 bytes of SRAM. Nearly every byte is spoken for, and the missing features are part of the design’s honest accounting.
